images.title: Same last digit
images.purpose: Show that 12 and 22 end in the same digit but only 12 is a multiple of 4.
images.composition: Two groups of dots side by side with wide space between, labels above and a note below each.
images.exact_structure: Left: 12 teal #0072B2 dots in 3 neat groups of 4. Right: 22 amber #E69F00 dots in 5 groups of 4 and 2 extra dots set apart in reddish purple #CC79A7. Number label above each group. Exactly 34 dots.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
groups that do not each hold exactly 4 dots
images.takeaway: The last digit alone cannot tell if a number is a multiple of 4.
images.description: Twelve dots make three full groups of 4; twenty two dots make five groups of 4 with 2 left over.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the groups of 4 in each picture and say what is left.

image_decisions.why: Two numbers with the same last digit and different results are a picture idea.
